payload.source_label: Equation (1.11): Riemann initial data is q_l for x below zero and q_r for x above zero

contract.statement: Equation (1.11) prescribes Riemann initial data: at time zero, the state equals a fixed left state at every negative position and a fixed right state at every positive position. The interface is chosen as zero, and its value is unspecified. The chapter supplies a real vector-valued state convention. The surrounding prose describes a single jump, although the displayed equation does not explicitly require distinct states. This initial-data prescription accompanies a hyperbolic equation and is not itself an evolution or solvability claim [printed page 1, state convention following (1.1); printed page 5, Section 1.2.1, opening paragraph and (1.11)].
assumptions: The surrounding problem is a hyperbolic equation with special piecewise-constant initial data [printed page 5, Section 1.2.1, opening paragraph].
The interface is placed at x = 0 by the source's choice 'say x = 0' [printed page 5, immediately before (1.11)].

The real vector-valued state convention is inherited from the chapter introduction; (1.11) does not restate the domain or component count [printed page 1, paragraph following (1.1); printed page 5, (1.11)].
The source describes a single jump, but the equation itself does not state q_l ≠ q_r [printed page 5, sentence preceding (1.11) and the displayed equation].

The neighboring-cell assignments q_l = Q_{i−1} and q_r = Q_i illustrate a finite-volume application and are not prerequisites for the general initial-data formula [printed page 5, paragraph following (1.11)].

The later discussion of similarity solutions and wave structure concerns the resulting Riemann solution, rather than additional branches or conditions in the initial-data equation [printed pages 5–6, paragraph following (1.11)].
quantifiers: x is the real spatial coordinate, with the two conditions understood for all x < 0 and all x > 0 [printed page 1, state domain following (1.1); printed page 5, (1.11)].
q is the state as a function of position and time; only its time-zero values are prescribed here [printed page 1, paragraph following (1.1); printed page 5, (1.11)].

q_l and q_r denote fixed left and right states in the state space of q; their state-space membership is inherited from the chapter's notation rather than separately quantified in (1.11) [printed page 1, q : R × R → R^m; printed page 5, (1.11)].
m denotes the number of real components of the state in the chapter's system notation [printed page 1, paragraph following (1.1)].
